capabilities: Synchronize the vault across desktop and mobile devices through a self-hosted Syncidian server
Back up each user's vault to a private GitHub repository as the durable source of truth
Expose vault search, reading, writing, and organizing to AI tools through a built-in MCP server
Detect and resolve sync conflicts with a keep-local/keep-remote/merge UI
Monitor devices, sync activity, and server health in a web dashboard
extras: The project is under active development; the README warns not to use early builds for critical or highly sensitive vaults. A managed hosted service is planned at $2/month but not yet available; self-hosting is free. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian. Install is also possible via BRAT or sideloading.
intentEvidence: Syncidian isn't trying to reproduce every feature of Obsidian Sync.
motivation: The author built it so that a vault belongs to its owner, is backed up by the owner, and is accessible to the AI tools the owner chooses, with self-hosting simple enough for anyone comfortable with Docker.
problem: Obsidian Sync is a paid closed service, and Git-based sync plugins depend on Node or a local git binary, so they never run on Android or iOS.
